etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English expense, from Anglo-Norman expense and Old French espense, from Late Latin expēnsa, from Latin expendō. See expend.

definitions.definition: A spending or consuming, often a disbursement of funds.
The elimination or consumption of something, sometimes with the notion of loss or damage to the thing eliminated.

quote.text: And moan the expense of many a vanished sight.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To charge a cost against an expense account; to bill something to the company for which one works.
